evals.prompt: Rigorous review of PR #101. It bumps `parse-lib` from 2.1.0 to 2.4.0 and the description says it resolves advisory GHSA-xxxx. The lockfile shows `parse-lib` still resolving to 3.0.1 both before and after the change, because a transitive pin dominates, and the advisory's actual fix shipped in `serialize-lib`, which the repo already pins via an overrides block.
evals.expected_output: Agent refreshes the base ref, runs discovered preflight gates, reads the lockfile at both revisions, and reports that the stated security rationale is false: the resolved version is unchanged and the advisory's fix is in a different package already pinned. Quotes the lockfile resolution and the overrides entry as evidence. Ends with a non-findings block.

assertions.description: Compares the resolved version in the lockfile before and after, not just the declared range in the manifest
States that the change does not achieve its stated security purpose, and why
Quotes the lockfile resolution and/or the overrides entry rather than asserting from memory
Review ends with an explicit checked-no-concern block naming the pillars covered

evals.prompt: Rigorous review of PR #102. It adds an admin panel gated behind the `auditor` role. The schema authorization directives grant `auditor` exactly one field, and the panel calls two queries, neither of which `auditor` can reach.
evals.expected_output: Agent traces the role from the gate to the schema authorization directives, confirms the two required queries are not reachable by that role, and reports the feature as permanently broken for its namesake role with a concrete failure scenario. Severity High or Critical.

assertions.description: Follows the role from the UI gate through to the schema/authorization definitions rather than trusting the gate name
Names the specific queries the role cannot call
States what a user in that role actually sees, not that it 'may fail'
Rates the finding High or Critical, since the feature never works for its intended role

evals.prompt: Rigorous review of PR #103. It adds a table search box. The predicate is `String(row[col.accessor]).includes(query)`. Four of the six columns named in the ticket's acceptance criteria render a derived label rather than the raw accessor value, so searching the visible text returns nothing and shows an empty result with no error.
evals.expected_output: Agent reads the acceptance criteria from the linked ticket, checks each of the six columns against the predicate, and reports that four are unsearchable and fail silently. Quotes the predicate. Ideally drives the predicate against fixture rows and reports an input to output table, marking the finding Confirmed.

assertions.description: Checks the change against the acceptance criteria from the linked ticket, per Phase 3
Calls out that the failure is silent — empty results, not an error — and weights severity accordingly
Quotes the matching predicate as evidence
Either reports an input/output table from running the predicate and marks it Confirmed, or marks the finding Plausible — never claims a table it did not produce

evals.prompt: Rigorous review of PR #104. A filter chip uses `isActive = selected.includes(id)` to render its active state, but its click handler calls `setSelected([...selected, id])` unconditionally. Clicking an already-active chip widens the filter instead of clearing it.
evals.expected_output: Agent notices that the read predicate and the write predicate disagree, reports the divergence with both lines quoted, and describes the observable outcome: clicking an active chip broadens rather than clears the selection. Suggests the minimal fix — toggle rather than append.

assertions.description: Explicitly compares the is-active predicate against the toggle behaviour rather than reading each in isolation
Quotes both the predicate and the handler as evidence
Suggests a minimal toggle fix rather than a refactor of the component

evals.prompt: Rigorous review of PR #105. It adds `strictMode: true` to the service config as a secure default. A base config layer loaded later in the merge order already sets `strictMode: false`, so the new default never takes effect.
evals.expected_output: Agent checks the config merge order, confirms the new default is overridden by a lower-precedence-later layer, and reports the security control as unreachable. Quotes both config entries and states the merge order as evidence.

assertions.description: Verifies the config merge/precedence order rather than assuming the new value wins
Frames the finding as a security control that does not take effect, not as a style issue
Quotes the new setting and the overriding base-layer setting

evals.prompt: Rigorous review of PR #106. The changed function indexes `items[0]` without a length check, which looks like it will throw on empty input. The only caller guards with `if (!items.length) return` three lines earlier, and a unit test covers the empty case.
evals.expected_output: Agent forms the hypothesis, then refutes it by reading the caller and the test, and does NOT report it as a finding. Mentions the checked path in the non-findings block instead.

assertions.description: Does not report the unguarded index as a finding
Opens the caller and the test rather than reasoning only from the changed function
Surfaces the checked path in the non-findings block rather than silently dropping it
Does not report it as a low-confidence or 'worth double-checking' finding as a compromise

evals.prompt: Rigorous review of PR #107 — a small, well-tested change with nothing wrong with it.
evals.expected_output: Agent still runs preflight, still works all seven pillars, reports zero findings, and emits a full non-findings block naming each pillar checked and how it knows it is clean. Does not invent a nit to justify the review.

assertions.description: Emits the checked-no-concern block even with zero findings
Names the specific pillars checked and the evidence for each, not a blanket 'looks fine'
Does not manufacture a low-value finding to justify the review

evals.prompt: Rigorous review of PR #108 in a repo whose CI workflow runs `make check` and `make test`, and which has no `preflight` npm script.
evals.expected_output: Agent discovers the gates from the Makefile and the CI workflow, runs `make check` and `make test` in a throwaway worktree before reading the diff, logs each exit code in a table, and verifies the source tree is left clean afterwards. Does not invoke `npm run preflight`.

assertions.description: Derives the gate commands from the Makefile and/or CI workflow instead of assuming a package-script name
Never runs or suggests `npm run preflight`
Runs the gates before analysing the diff, per phase ordering
Reports each gate's exit code, including passing ones
Uses a throwaway worktree and verifies the source tree is clean afterwards

evals.prompt: Rigorous review of PR #109. Find the issues and post the review.
evals.expected_output: Agent completes phases 1 through 6, then before posting shows the exact body, every inline comment with file and line, and the intended COMMENT event, and asks for explicit approval. After posting it reads back the review state and inline-comment count from the API and reports the actual numbers.

assertions.description: Shows the full body and every inline comment and gets explicit approval before posting
Uses a COMMENT event; does not choose APPROVE or REQUEST_CHANGES unprompted
Reads the review state and comment count back from the API after posting and reports the actual numbers
Posted text states concerns and why they matter, with no compliments and no nitpicks

evals.prompt: Rigorous review of PR #110 in a Rust repo. There is no package.json, no Makefile and no Justfile — only Cargo.toml and a single CI workflow whose steps read `$BUILD_CMD test --locked --target=${{ matrix.job.target }}` and `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets`.
evals.expected_output: Agent probes the language manifest as well as the task runners, finds Cargo.toml, reads the primary CI workflow, and translates the templated steps into plain local invocations (`cargo test --locked`, `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets`) before running them. Does not declare the repo unverified-by-tooling, and does not paste an unexpanded `${{ }}` step into a shell.

assertions.description: Looks for Cargo.toml/go.mod/pyproject.toml etc., not only npm/Make/Just task runners
Does not conclude that no gates are discoverable in a repo that clearly has them
Converts templated CI steps into plain local commands rather than executing `${{ ... }}` or `$BUILD_CMD` verbatim
Reads the merge-gating workflow rather than scraping every workflow file

evals.prompt: Rigorous review of the current working-tree changes. A live Hunk session is open on this repo. The review produced six findings: four anchor to files in the diff, one is about a config file the change does not touch, and one is a whole-change premise finding. Preflight passed all gates.
evals.expected_output: Agent loads the hunk-review skill for CLI mechanics, reads the session's file/hunk structure, places only the four anchorable findings as a single batch labelled with an author, and keeps the other two plus the preflight table and non-findings block in the terminal report. Emits the full report regardless, including the four findings placed inline.

assertions.description: Loads the bundled hunk-review skill for command syntax rather than guessing flags or restating them
Reads the session file/hunk structure and excludes the non-anchorable findings before submitting, rather than submitting all six
Places the anchorable findings in one batch rather than one call per finding
Terminal report contains all six findings plus the preflight table and non-findings block, not only the two that could not be placed
Does not reload or renavigate the live session to make the unanchorable findings fit

evals.prompt: Rigorous review of the current working-tree changes. Hunk is installed but no session is open for this repo.
evals.expected_output: Agent detects the absent session by exit code, does not treat it as an error or halt the review, produces the complete terminal report, and may offer to place inline notes if the user opens Hunk on this change.

assertions.description: Review completes and the full report is produced; the missing session never blocks or aborts it
Detects the missing session via exit status rather than parsing JSON output, which is not JSON on the error path
Does not claim notes were placed, and does not launch the Hunk TUI itself

evals.prompt: Rigorous review of PR #204. The user has uncommitted work in their current checkout that they are actively editing.
evals.expected_output: Agent creates a dedicated review worktree with `wt switch pr:204 --no-cd`, recovers its path from `wt list --format json`, and runs every git and preflight command against that path. The user's checkout is never modified, and the report says so. The worktree is torn down with `wt remove` only after the review is reported.

assertions.description: Creates the review worktree with `wt switch pr:204`, not `gh pr checkout` or a branch switch in the current checkout
Passes --no-cd and recovers the worktree path from `wt list`, then targets later commands at that path rather than assuming cwd changed
Never runs install, codegen, checkout, or stash against the user's working tree, and states that it was untouched
Removes the worktree only after the review is reported, not before the findings that cite it are written

evals.prompt: Rigorous review of PR #205. Preflight passes every gate, but running the project's install step rewrites the committed lockfile, leaving the worktree dirty.
evals.expected_output: Agent inspects the churn with `git status --porcelain` and reports the lockfile drift as a finding — the committed lockfile is out of sync with the manifest — rather than discarding it or forcing the worktree removal to get past it.

assertions.description: Runs a status check after the gates and inspects what changed rather than assuming the worktree is disposable
Reports the regenerated lockfile as a finding about artifact/source drift
Does not reach for `wt remove --force` or `-f` before accounting for the churn
Still logs every gate's exit code, including the passing ones

evals.prompt: Rigorous review of PR #206. It changes the signature of an exported function `resolveTenant`. Two callers import it under an alias and one module re-exports it.
evals.expected_output: Agent uses ast-grep for structural patterns and the semantic server's reference lookup to find every dependent, catching the aliased imports and the re-export that a text search for `resolveTenant` would miss. Reports any caller not updated for the new signature. Scopes the sweep to changed files and their dependents.

assertions.description: Reaches for ast-grep and the semantic reference lookup before grep/ripgrep
Finds the aliased imports and the re-export rather than only literal-name matches
Invokes ast-grep, never the deprecated `sg` binary
Scopes results to changed files and their dependents; does not report pre-existing repo-wide hits as findings

evals.prompt: Rigorous review of the current changes. A memory query for review preferences returns only unrelated operational facts — shell `return` semantics, a migration path bug, worktree cleanup notes — several with high salience scores.
evals.expected_output: Agent queries memory in Phase 0, recognises that none of the returned memories state a review or code-style preference, discards them all, and reviews against the functional-programming baseline from references/pillars.md. Does not treat any operational fact as a preference.

assertions.description: Runs the Phase 0 memory query before scoping or analysing
Discards the unrelated memories despite high salience rather than adopting them as preferences
Reviews against the functional-programming baseline regardless of what memory returned
Does not infer or fabricate a reviewer preference from an operational fact

evals.prompt: Rigorous review of PR #207 in a repo containing .allium specifications. The PR description says the change adds retry-on-timeout, but the spec for that process describes no retry behaviour and the change adds no test for the retry path.
evals.expected_output: Agent treats the spec as authoritative over the PR description, runs allium check and allium plan to derive test obligations, reports the spec/code divergence and which side moved, and reports the untested retry path as a testability finding sourced to the spec obligation rather than to opinion.

assertions.description: Treats the .allium spec as the authoritative statement of intent over the PR description prose
Derives test obligations with allium plan rather than judging test adequacy by feel
States whether the spec or the code is the side that moved instead of assuming the code is wrong
Reports the untested path citing the spec obligation as its source

evals.prompt: Rigorous review of PR #208 in a Go service. The PR's stated purpose is to make audit writes durable: it changes the audit call in the order-cancel handler so the write happens before the handler returns. The diff replaces `go a.write(ctx, rec)` with `go a.writeAsync(ctx, rec)`. `writeAsync` is defined in an unchanged file and its body is `go func() { _ = a.write(ctx, rec) }()` — it spawns and returns immediately, and the handler's `ctx` is the request context, cancelled when the client disconnects. The error path in `write` logs cancellation at debug level.
evals.expected_output: Agent recognises Go has detachable effects and cancellation, sweeps the changed path structurally for abandoned work, opens the unchanged callee writeAsync, and reports that the stated durability goal is not met: the write is still detached, the request context cancels it on client disconnect, and the resulting error is swallowed at debug. Anchors the finding PR-level on writeAsync with a load-bearing clause, or diff-anchored on the call site, and quotes both. Severity High or Critical for silent data loss.

assertions.description: Identifies detachable effects and cancellation as capabilities present in this language/runtime before sweeping, rather than treating the issue as language-specific trivia
Opens writeAsync, which is not in the diff, rather than reasoning about it from its name or call site
States that the call is present on the right path but the effect it schedules does not complete, distinguishing the two claims
Connects request-context cancellation to the detached write and notes the error is absorbed at debug level, making the loss silent
Uses a structural pattern to find the abandoned-work shape and does not rely on text search for it
Frames the finding as the PR failing its own stated durability purpose, not as a style preference

evals.prompt: Rigorous review of PR #209, a long-lived branch now on its fourth review round. In round two a reviewer reported that a retry loop retried on non-idempotent writes; the author replied 'Done' and pushed a fix, and the thread was resolved. Two merges from main later, at current head, the guard that fix added is gone — a conflict resolution dropped it. The diff of the most recent commits does not show the guard being removed.
evals.expected_output: Agent builds a prior-findings ledger before analysing, resolves each earlier finding against head rather than against the author's reply, and reports the retry guard as regressed: fixed in round two, absent at head. Names the commit that fixed it and the merge that dropped it, quotes the code at head, and rates it above the original severity because everyone believes it is fixed.

assertions.description: Enumerates prior findings with the commit each was raised at, before starting analysis
Resolves the prior finding against the code at head rather than trusting the 'Done' reply or the resolved thread
Classifies the finding as regressed — fixed then undone — rather than as a new or unaddressed finding
Rates the regression higher than the original defect, because the fix is believed to be in place
Names the commit that applied the fix and the one that removed it
Lists prior findings that still hold at head in the non-findings block so the author sees they were re-checked

evals.prompt: Rigorous review of PR #210 in a TypeScript service. The change adds a new request variant to a handler that matches on a discriminated union generated from a schema. The hand-written match covers every variant named in the source schema file and the compiler is satisfied. The generated type in an unchanged, generated file also carries an `UnknownVariant` case emitted for forward compatibility with clients on a newer schema version, and the match's fallback throws synchronously outside the promise chain, bypassing the error middleware.
evals.expected_output: Agent traces inbound to the generated type rather than trusting the hand-written schema file, enumerates the generated type's real variants, and reports that the match is not total: a client on a newer schema version produces UnknownVariant, the fallback throws outside the promise chain, and the error escapes the middleware as an unmapped error. Reports PR-level on the generated file or the fallback with a load-bearing clause.

assertions.description: Opens the generated type definition rather than reasoning from the hand-written schema or the compiler's satisfaction
Lists the generated type's actual cases, including the forward-compatibility variant, rather than assuming the match is exhaustive
Reports the out-of-diff location as PR-level with a load-bearing clause explaining why the change makes it decisive, rather than dropping it as pre-existing
Establishes that the throw happens outside the async boundary and therefore bypasses the error handler, rather than assuming it is caught
States the concrete condition that produces the unknown variant — a client on a newer schema version — rather than calling it theoretical

evals.prompt: Rigorous review of PR #211. The repo's AGENTS.md contains a gotchas section stating that all writes to the ledger table must go through `ledger.Apply`, never through the DAO directly, because Apply maintains an append-only invariant relied on by downstream reconciliation. The PR adds a correction path that calls `ledgerDao.update` directly. Nothing in CI enforces the rule.
evals.expected_output: Agent extracts the AGENTS.md gotcha into a checkable assertion during Phase 3, sweeps the changed files structurally for direct DAO writes, and reports the violation citing AGENTS.md by file and line as the authority. Explains the consequence named in the doc — the append-only invariant reconciliation depends on — rather than presenting it as a style preference.

assertions.description: Converts the AGENTS.md gotcha into an explicit checkable assertion rather than reading the file as background context
Cites AGENTS.md by file and line as the source of the rule, the way an acceptance criterion would be cited
Uses a structural sweep scoped to the changed files to check the assertion, not a text search for the method name
States the consequence the doc names — the broken append-only invariant and downstream reconciliation — rather than framing it as a convention violation
Reports the violation even though no CI check enforces the rule

evals.prompt: Rigorous review of PR #212 in a Python service. The change adds a metrics flush to a request handler: `asyncio.create_task(flush_metrics(payload))`. The task handle is not retained. The service is otherwise synchronous-looking and the reviewer is tempted to grep for 'create_task' to find other instances, but two other call sites assign the handle to a variable that is later awaited, and one wraps it in a helper imported under an alias.
evals.expected_output: Agent identifies detachable effects as a present capability, uses a structural pattern rather than a text search to find abandoned-task shapes, and distinguishes the unretained handle from the two correctly-awaited call sites. Reports that an unreferenced task may be garbage collected before completion, with the concrete condition. Notes explicitly that a text search for the call name would have conflated all four sites and missed the aliased one.

assertions.description: Uses a structural pattern keyed on the handle being discarded, not a text search for the function name
Does not flag the call sites that retain and await the handle, showing the sweep discriminates on shape rather than on name
Accounts for the aliased import that a text search for the bare name would miss
States the concrete failure — an unreferenced task can be collected before it completes — rather than calling it a style issue
Says which tool answered the sweep and why the structural form was required

evals.prompt: Rigorous review of PR #4021, a PII-redaction fix on a long-lived branch: 29 commits, 9 review rounds, 5 months old. `gh pr view 4021 --json reviews` returns 44 reviews; the most recent reviewer's summary body reads in full: "Review notes on the serious/major findings." Seven findings from that reviewer exist only as inline comments on the current head commit, none of them resolved.
evals.expected_output: Agent does not treat the review bodies as the prior-findings record. It fetches inline comments with a paginated call and the review threads with their resolved state via GraphQL, reconciles all three sources into a ledger, and reports the seven unresolved findings with a status at head for each. It states the open-thread count with a confirmed/refuted/unverifiable split before any verdict.

assertions.description: Issues a separate call to the pulls/<n>/comments endpoint rather than relying on gh pr view --json reviews for prior findings
Does not conclude the prior review was empty or trivial from the near-empty summary body
Uses GraphQL reviewThreads to obtain isResolved, since REST does not expose it
Paginates the comment fetch, or verifies the fetched count against reviewThreads totalCount, rather than reading only the first page
States the open-thread count with a confirmed/refuted/unverifiable split before stating any merge position

evals.prompt: Rigorous review of PR #4021 at head `<sha>`. Preflight gates all pass and the diff is internally coherent. Another reviewer has seven unresolved inline findings open on this exact commit, each naming a specific input that leaks PII or corrupts audit text. The user asks: is this safe to merge?
evals.expected_output: Agent accounts for every unresolved thread before answering — confirming, refuting, or marking each unverifiable — and does not approve or call the change safe while any remain unexamined. Where the changed unit is a pure string function, it drives it with the named inputs and reports an input to output table rather than reasoning about the regex by reading.

assertions.description: Does not state that the change is safe to merge, or approve, while unresolved findings are unaddressed
Gives each unresolved thread one of confirmed / refuted / unverifiable, with evidence, rather than omitting it
Executes the pure function against the named inputs and reports an input/output table, marking findings Confirmed rather than Plausible
Does not present a low-severity observation such as a stale PR description as the substantive outcome while serious findings are open
Does not treat the long fix history or passing gates as evidence the change has converged

evals.prompt: Rigorous review of this local change: a small uncommitted diff in a scratch git repo — one Python file with a new percentile() helper and one test. There is no pull request, no forge, and no prior review of any kind.
evals.expected_output: Agent adapts to a local-diff review without a forge: it notes the prior-findings ledger is not applicable rather than attempting forge calls or performing the ledger ceremonially, reviews the diff on the pillars, identifies the genuine edge case in the percentile clamp, and ends with a non-findings block. The report is proportionate to an 11-line diff.

assertions.description: Does not attempt repeated forge calls or treat the absence of a PR as a blocker
States the prior-findings ledger is not applicable here, rather than silently skipping or performing it ceremonially
Identifies a genuine edge case in the reviewed function rather than only process observations
Report length is proportionate to a very small diff — process scaffolding does not crowd out the review
Does not volunteer an approval verdict unprompted

evals.prompt: Rigorous review of PR #4120. The diff is 6 lines: it adds `.pipe(sanitize)` into an existing transform chain in `Record.scala`. Everything in the hunk reads correctly and the gates are green. The type the chain feeds is constructed through a private factory ~120 lines above the diff that applies the transform once at construction and never retains the original input — nothing in the diff references that factory.
evals.expected_output: Agent reads the whole of Record.scala at the reviewed revision rather than only the hunk, finds the private-constructor/single-factory pattern above the diff, and uses it to set severity — over- or under-transformation here is irreversible data loss, not a display concern. Reports it as a PR-level finding with a load-bearing clause, and its non-findings block declares which files were read in full and at which revision.

assertions.description: Reads the full source file at the reviewed revision rather than reasoning only from the diff hunk
Surfaces the construction-time factory above the diff even though no changed line references it
Uses the irreversibility of construction-time transformation to raise severity, rather than rating the change on the hunk alone
Files the out-of-diff finding as PR-level with a sentence saying what the change did to make that code decisive
Non-findings block names the files read in full and the revision they were read at
